target.title: fix: skip setup-only channel plugins in outbound resolution and drain pending deliveries on qqbot reconnect
target.body:
## Summary

When the qqbot WebSocket reconnects after a session timeout (close code `4009`), `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()` returns a setup-only plugin stub that lacks any send capability. This causes the `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` error, and all messages queued during the disconnection window are permanently lost.

## Root Cause

`resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()` resolves the first matching plugin entry for a channel id without verifying that the entry actually has send capability (`outbound.sendText`, `message.send.text`, etc.). During qqbot WebSocket reconnection, a setup-only plugin entry (registered for configuration/pairing but not for message delivery) shadows the real sending plugin, causing the resolution to short-circuit with a non-functional stub.

Regression introduced in 2026.5.28 (commit `e932160`).

## Fix

### 1. Split outbound channel resolution into shared and delivery paths (`channel-resolution.ts`)

Add a `channelPluginCanSend()` predicate that checks for any of the 10 known send methods across both the legacy `outbound` adapter and the newer `message.send` adapter:

- `outbound.sendText / sendMedia / sendPayload / sendPoll / sendFormattedText / sendFormattedMedia`
- `message.send.text / media / payload / poll`

Instead of gating the shared `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()` resolver (which would break action-only channel plugins that have `actions.handleAction` but no send capability), a new **`resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()`** resolver applies the send-capability guard exclusively for message delivery paths.

- **`resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()`**: Shared resolver — returns any matching plugin regardless of send capability, preserving resolution for action dispatch, target resolution, and other non-send callers.
- **`resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()`**: Delivery resolver — skips setup-only entries and only returns plugins that can actually send messages.
- **`resolveOutboundChannelMessageAdapter()`**: Updated to use the delivery resolver.
- **`message.ts`**: `sendMessage`/`sendPoll` updated to use the delivery resolver.

### 2. Align the direct delivery path with the operation-aware resolver (`deliver.ts`)

The preflight resolver was operation-aware, but the actual direct delivery handler reloaded the adapter capability-blind: `createChannelHandler` → `loadBootstrappedOutboundAdapter` → `loadChannelOutboundAdapter` resolved the first registry entry for the channel id (`createChannelRegistryLoader((entry) => entry.plugin.outbound)`) without checking send capability. A setup-only shell with a defined-but-non-send `outbound` (`{ deliveryMode: "direct" }`, no `sendText`) pinned ahead of the runtime sender therefore still shadowed the real adapter on the direct send path, throwing `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` even after preflight had selected a valid plugin. This also affected the reconnect drain path, which has no preflight.

`loadBootstrappedOutboundAdapter` now resolves through the same `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()` resolver as preflight (with `allowBootstrap`, operation `text`), so preflight and the actual direct delivery handler share one send-capability-aware resolution path. The previous manual bootstrap-and-retry is removed because the resolver's `allowBootstrap` performs the equivalent lazy materialize-then-retry. The generic registry loader and the CLI/SDK surfaces are left untouched.

### 3. Drain pending deliveries on qqbot reconnect (`extensions/qqbot/src/channel.ts`)

The `onReady` and `onResumed` gateway callbacks now call `drainPendingDeliveries()` from the plugin SDK delivery queue runtime, recovering messages that were queued while the WebSocket was disconnected. The drain is:

- Filtered by channel (`qqbot`) and account id, with a fallback for default-account entries where `accountId` may be `undefined`
- Deduplicated via `drainKey` to prevent concurrent drains
- Wrapped in try/catch so drain failures do not break the reconnection flow

### 4. Route the gateway poll handler through the operation-aware resolver (`src/gateway/server-methods/send.ts`)

The gateway `poll` handler still resolved its outbound plugin via the operation-blind `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()`, while `sendPoll` (`message.ts`) and the direct text delivery path (`deliver.ts`) already routed through the operation-aware `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()`. This left the gateway poll endpoint as the last surface where a setup-only / text-only first-match plugin could shadow a poll-capable runtime fallback and force a spurious `"unsupported poll channel"`, even though the new resolver test proves the poll-capable fallback should win.

The poll handler now resolves through `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery({ operation: "poll", allowBootstrap: true })`, mirroring the text delivery path. The `durationSeconds` / `isAnonymous` capability checks below the resolution now read from the same poll-capable plugin that serves `sendPoll`, so the capability gate and the actual send no longer disagree. The two non-poll resolver call sites in the same file (the `send` and `action` surfaces) are intentionally left on the shared resolver, since action-only plugins must still resolve without send capability.

## Tests

- `channel-resolution.test.ts`: setup-only plugin returns from shared resolver, action-only plugin resolves from shared but not delivery resolver, delivery resolver skips setup-only and returns sending fallback, legacy outbound adapter, poll-only outbound
- `deliver.test.ts`: new unmocked regression driving the real `deliverOutboundPayloads` → `createChannelHandler` → `loadBootstrappedOutboundAdapter` path with a pinned setup-only shell that exposes a defined non-send `outbound` plus an active send-capable fallback, asserting the send-capable adapter actually delivers (fails before the Fix 2 alignment with `"Outbound not configured"`, passes after)
- `channel.test.ts`: onReady drain, onResumed drain

Fixes #88955.


## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: After a QQ Bot WebSocket disconnect (session takeover / close code 4009), `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()` returned a setup-only plugin stub instead of the runtime entry, causing `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` and dropping all pending deliveries.

- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw `2026.6.2` (commit `b90683e`, branch `fix/qqbot-reconnect-outbound-88955`), macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0. QQ Bot plugin `@openclaw/qqbot@2026.5.31-beta.4` with live QQ Bot credentials (appId `<redacted>`).

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  1. Built patched OpenClaw from fix branch: `pnpm build && npm pack --ignore-scripts`
  2. Installed globally: `npm install -g openclaw-2026.6.2.tgz` — confirmed version: `OpenClaw 2026.6.2 (b90683e)`
  3. Restarted gateway: `openclaw gateway restart`
  4. Observed qqbot plugin startup, WebSocket connection, and `Gateway ready` callback sequence in logs
  5. Verified normal QQ Bot C2C message round-trip: user sent "hello" → bot received → processed → replied with markdown (20 chars, 200 OK)
  6. Scanned full gateway log for `"Outbound not configured"` errors — zero matches
  7. Repeated restart cycle to confirm reconnect stability across multiple `Gateway ready` events

- **Evidence after fix**:
  ```
  # Patched OpenClaw installed and running
  $ openclaw --version
  OpenClaw 2026.6.2 (b90683e)

  # Gateway restart sequence — qqbot reconnects cleanly
  2026-06-02T22:38:53.727+08:00 [gateway] received SIGTERM; restarting
  2026-06-02T22:39:15.986+08:00 [gateway] http server listening (8 plugins: ..., qqbot, ...; 1.6s)
  2026-06-02T22:39:16.171+08:00 [qqbot] [qqbot:default] Starting gateway — appId=<redacted>, enabled=true
  2026-06-02T22:39:17.387+08:00 [qqbot] [default] Connecting to wss://api.sgroup.qq.com/websocket
  2026-06-02T22:39:18.468+08:00 [qqbot] [default] WebSocket connected
  2026-06-02T22:39:18.641+08:00 [qqbot] [qqbot:default] Gateway ready

  # Successful QQ Bot message delivery after reconnect
  2026-06-02T22:32:40.229+08:00 [qqbot] [default] Processing message from <redacted>: hello
  2026-06-02T22:32:59.431+08:00 [qqbot] [default] [qqbot:api] <<< Status: 200 OK
  2026-06-02T22:32:59.432+08:00 [qqbot] [default] Sent markdown chunk (20/20 chars) with 0 HTTP images (c2c)

  # Zero outbound resolution errors across entire log history
  $ grep -c "Outbound not configured.*qqbot" ~/Library/Logs/openclaw/gateway.log
  0

  # Multiple Gateway ready events over 4+ hours — all clean reconnects
  $ grep "qqbot.*Gateway ready" ~/Library/Logs/openclaw/gateway.log | wc -l
  18
  ```

- **Observed result after fix**: The delivery resolver correctly skipped the setup-only plugin entry (which has no `sendText`/`sendMedia` methods) and resolved the runtime entry with full send capability. Outbound messages delivered successfully through the QQ Bot API (HTTP 200). Zero occurrences of the `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` error across 18 reconnect cycles over a 4+ hour observation window. The shared resolver continued to return all plugin entries for non-send callers (action dispatch, target resolution), preserving action-only plugin compatibility.

- **Direct delivery path alignment (follow-up)**: A reviewer noted that the preflight fix did not cover the actual direct delivery handler construction, which reloaded the adapter capability-blind and could still let a pinned setup-only shell shadow the runtime sender. `loadBootstrappedOutboundAdapter` now routes through the same `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()` resolver as preflight. Verified locally on the fix branch (macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0): the new unmocked `deliver.test.ts` regression fails before the alignment (`Error: Outbound not configured for channel: matrix` thrown from `createChannelHandler`) and passes after; full focused suite green (`channel-resolution`, `message`, `message.channels`, `deliver`, qqbot `channel` — 169 tests passing), `pnpm tsgo:prod` and `pnpm tsgo:test` clean, `pnpm build` clean, `git diff --check` clean, lint clean.

- **Gateway poll resolver alignment (follow-up)**: A reviewer noted the gateway poll endpoint (`src/gateway/server-methods/send.ts`) still used the operation-blind `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()`, so a setup-only / text-only first match could shadow a poll-capable fallback and return `"unsupported poll channel"` despite a working poll plugin existing. The poll handler now routes through `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery({ operation: "poll", allowBootstrap: true })`, matching `sendPoll` and the direct text delivery path. Verified locally on the fix branch (macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0): a new gateway `send.test.ts` regression where the first-match plugin is a text-only shell (no `sendPoll`) and a poll-capable plugin is registered as the runtime fallback — the handler now skips the shell and dispatches the poll via the fallback (`messageId: poll-fallback-1`) instead of returning `"unsupported poll channel"`; the test fails under the old operation-blind resolver and passes after the change. Full gateway send suite green (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/send.test.ts` — 124 tests passing), `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:test:src` clean. The two non-poll resolver call sites in the same file are intentionally untouched.

- **What was not tested**:

  Live drain proof is not reproducible on the fixed build. The `drainReconnectPendingDeliveries()` mechanism (Fix 2) was verified via unit tests but not observed draining actual queued entries in a live environment. This is not an oversight — it is a structural consequence of the resolver fix (Fix 1) eliminating the only deterministic cause of pending qqbot entries. Code-level analysis confirms this:

  **How the delivery queue works** (`deliver.ts:1254-1280`): Every outbound delivery is write-ahead enqueued via `enqueueDelivery()` before any send attempt. On success, `ackDelivery()` removes the entry (`deliver.ts:1367`). On throw, `failDelivery()` bumps `retryCount` and **leaves it pending** (`delivery-queue-storage.ts:137-144`).

  **What created the pending entries in #88955**: The `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` throw fired from `createChannelHandler` (`deliver.ts:223-231`) when `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery` returned a setup-only plugin with no send methods. This throw occurs **outside** the per-payload try/catch (`deliver.ts:1451`), so it propagated to the queue-cleanup catch → `failDelivery` → entry left pending. The resolver fix eliminates this throw by filtering setup-only entries via `channelPluginCanSend()`.

  **Why transient QQ API failures also do not create pending entries**: The qqbot engine **swallows** HTTP/network errors into returned `{error}` result objects instead of throwing (`outbound.ts:301-304, 313-318`). The delivery core text branch records "sent" purely on `deliveredResults.length > 0` with no message-id identity gate (`deliver.ts:1772-1778`), so a swallowed engine error yields a "sent" outcome → `ackDelivery` → entry removed, not pending.

  **The drain's real value**: It is a belt-and-suspenders safeguard for the **upgrade path** — entries left pending (with `lastError: "Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"`) by an unfixed build are drained immediately after a fixed gateway reconnects. The `bypassBackoff` predicate explicitly matches this exact error string (`/outbound not configured/i`), ensuring these entries skip retry backoff and are retried on the first reconnect event. If the retry still fails (e.g., the plugin is genuinely misconfigured), `isPermanentDeliveryError` (`delivery-queue-recovery.ts:79`) moves the entry to `failed/` — no infinite retry loop. `MAX_RETRIES` is also enforced before the bypass branch (`delivery-queue-recovery.ts:544`). The drain also covers the narrow crash-in-enqueue-to-ack window handled by `recoverPendingDeliveries` at startup (`delivery-queue-recovery.ts:604`). The drain selection filter (`channel === "qqbot"` + account id match + bypassBackoff for `"Outbound not configured"`, `channel.test.ts:90-152`) and the reconnect-drain integration logic (`delivery-queue.reconnect-drain.test.ts`) are exercised by 35 unit tests (all passing).

  **Seeded pending-drain proof**: To validate the drain recovery path end-to-end, a pending delivery entry was manually seeded into the SQLite delivery queue to simulate the upgrade scenario (entries left by an unfixed build):

  1. Inserted a pending entry: `id=seeded-drain-test-001`, `channel=qqbot`, `accountId=default`, `lastError="Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"`, `retry_count=1`
  2. Restarted gateway: `openclaw gateway restart`
  3. Observed recovery sequence in logs:

  ```
  00:30:00.353 [gateway] http server listening (8 plugins: ..., qqbot, ...; 1.9s)
  00:30:00.987 [delivery-recovery] Found 1 pending delivery entries — starting recovery
  00:30:01.567 [qqbot] [qqbot:api] <<< Status: 200 OK
  00:30:02.703 [delivery-recovery] Recovered delivery seeded-drain-test-001 on qqbot
  00:30:02.703 [delivery-recovery] Delivery recovery complete: 1 recovered, 0 failed, 0 skipped (max retries), 0 deferred (backoff)
  00:30:02.816 [qqbot] [default] WebSocket connected
  00:30:02.952 [qqbot] [qqbot:default] Gateway ready
  ```

  4. Verified entry removed from DB: `SELECT count(*) FROM delivery_queue_entries WHERE channel='qqbot' AND status='pending'` → **0**
  5. Zero `"Outbound not configured"` errors after restart

  **Key observation**: The `0 deferred (backoff)` in the recovery summary confirms the `bypassBackoff` predicate (`/outbound not configured/i`) correctly matched the seeded entry's `lastError`, allowing immediate retry without waiting for backoff. The entry was successfully delivered (HTTP 200) and acked (removed from queue).

  **Note**: The startup `recoverPendingDeliveries` path (`delivery-queue-recovery.ts:604`) executed before the qqbot `onReady` callback (`00:30:00.987` vs `00:30:02.952`), so startup recovery handled the entry before the reconnect drain fired. Both paths share the same underlying drain logic and bypass predicates; the startup path simply runs first. A naturally-occurring live drain on the `onReady` path cannot be reliably reproduced because the fix removes the deterministic failure that created those entries, and startup recovery pre-empts the reconnect drain for entries present at boot. Multi-shard configurations were not tested.

## Summary

- Extends `claws update <claw-or-agent> --from <source> --yes` behind `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1` to apply every grouped owner in `openclaw.clawUpdateResult.v1`.
- Rebuilds and compares the read-only plan immediately before mutation, then advances root package/version/integrity provenance only after all owner executors succeed.
- Applies managed workspace file add/change/remove through fs-safe rooted I/O with source digest checks, destination compare-and-swap checks, ownership updates, and guarded rollback.
- Applies MCP add/change/remove through the validated config writer with create-only or expected-value CAS, including remote `sse` / `streamable-http` declarations and credential-free `auth: "oauth"`.
- Applies cron add/change/remove through gateway-owned APIs. Changes must converge on the stable Claw declaration key and existing scheduler id.
- Applies exact ClawHub skill/plugin package versions and updates package references. Removing a reference never implies shared uninstall; conflicting shared plugin version pins fail closed.
- Rolls completed owners back in reverse order when a later owner or root provenance fails. Thrown config/gateway writes and package installs without artifact rollback report `update_partial` instead of claiming atomicity.
- Keeps `--dry-run` read-only and requires explicit `--yes` consent.

Stack references:
- RFC: openclaw/rfcs#27
- Base PR: openclaw/openclaw#102959
- Control UI plugin management alignment: openclaw/openclaw#103176

## Ownership and Control UI alignment

Package references remain per-Claw provenance over shared skill/plugin artifacts. Update-time package removal releases only this Claw's reference. A plugin pinned to a different version by another Claw is not replaced. This keeps CLI lifecycle behavior aligned with the shared uninstall/reference-warning model used by the Control UI rather than creating a second plugin ownership system.

Portable MCP declarations continue to use the validated config surface. They are separate from the Control UI's curated connector shelf and do not persist headers, tokens, or completed OAuth state.

## Real behavior proof

Environment: WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 with isolated config and state.

An installed `@acme/update-proof@1.1.0` agent was previewed and updated to `1.2.0`:

```bash
openclaw claws update update-proof --from ./target-grouped --dry-run --json
openclaw claws update update-proof --from ./target-grouped --yes --json
openclaw claws status update-proof --json
```

The target changed the agent, added `SOUL.md` and `NOTES.md`, and added a remote `streamable-http` OAuth MCP server.

Observed:
- preview reported four unblocked grouped actions;
- apply returned `openclaw.clawUpdateResult.v1` with `status: "complete"`;
- both workspace files matched their target digests;
- the MCP ownership record was `complete` and live state was `present`;
- status reported version `1.2.0`, zero partial records, zero drift, and zero unresolved MCP references;
- the original `addedAtMs` was preserved while `updatedAtMs` advanced.

Cron convergence and exact package installer behavior are covered with injected gateway/installer tests to avoid mutating a developer gateway or shared plugin installation during local proof.

## Validation

- 133 Claw, CLI, lifecycle, config, executor, rollback, and end-to-end tests across 19 files
- non-incremental core TypeScript check: `tsgo -p tsconfig.json --noEmit --incremental false`
- real isolated grouped preview -> consented apply -> status round trip
- `git diff --check`

target.title: fix: antml:/mm: namespaced tool-call XML leaks into chat replies (#97750)
target.body:
Closes #97750

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users on any deployment that serves a Claude model through an anthropic-messages-compatible proxy would see raw tool-call XML in their chat replies, and sometimes get no usable answer at all, when the proxy intermittently degraded a native `tool_use` block into plain text.

In that degraded case the model's tool call arrives as the Anthropic namespaced XML dialect — an optional `function_calls` wrapper containing `antml:invoke` / `antml:parameter` tags that use `name="..."` attributes (MiniMax emits the same shape with an `mm:` prefix). The harness did not recognize the namespace prefix or the attribute form anywhere, so the entire block leaked into the user-visible message instead of being executed, and a turn whose whole body was unrecognized markup could end with no real reply.

A follow-up fix in this PR also closes a streaming-only variant of the same leak: the final repair parser accepts whitespace-flexible attribute-dialect invoke tags (optional whitespace after `<`, around the `name` attribute, and around `=`), but the streamed-prefix recognizer only kept the exact `<ns>invoke name="` form buffered. A grammar-legal split form such as `<invoke name = "exec">` was therefore classified impossible mid-stream and flushed as raw visible text before final-message repair could promote it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The degraded tool call should never reach the user: it should either be executed or, failing that, hidden. This change teaches both layers that own that contract about the namespaced attribute dialect, using a closed namespace allow-list (`antml:`, `mm:`) factored into a single reused fragment — mirroring the existing reasoning-tag handling — so arbitrary `ns:` prefixes are not matched.

- Visible-text sanitizer: the tag-name scan now skips a known namespace prefix before reading the local tag name, and the quick-check / payload-start patterns accept the same optional prefix, so a namespaced wrapper is stripped on the same opt-in paths as the bare dialect.
- Repair/promotion layer: the repair grammar now promotes the attribute dialect (`invoke name="..."` / `parameter name="..."`, optionally namespaced, optionally wrapped in `function_calls`) back into an executed tool call, including the streaming and over-cap paths. Parameterless/self-closing invokes are never promoted, parameter values stay literal, and the existing payload-size limits are honored.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: `isViableXmlishInvokeOpenPrefix` is rewritten as a phase scanner that mirrors the final parser grammar one token at a time, so a buffer that ends partway through any phase of a grammar-legal invoke open (including whitespace-split forms) stays buffered instead of leaking, while the existing tool-name gating is preserved unchanged.
- Internal delivery paths become code-aware without changing the public contract: the low-level `packages/tool-call-repair` stripper takes an optional code-region predicate, threaded in from the delivery pipeline, `sanitizeUserFacingText`, and the visible-text sanitizer, so a complete invoke block inside a fenced or inline code span is no longer silently removed on those internal paths.
- The exported plugin SDK helper `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` stays strict by default (it scrubs tool-call-shaped blocks even inside code regions, matching current main), preserving the upgrade contract for third-party callers that use it to sanitize untrusted visible text. Code-aware behavior is available as an explicit opt-in via `{ preserveCodeRegions: true }`; the default remains a strict scrubber.

Non-goals/boundaries: the Anthropic and DSML transports are intentionally untouched (the native path is correct; the failure is degraded text owned by the repair package and sanitizer); the exported SDK helper's default behavior is unchanged from main (strict), with code-awareness added only as an opt-in and to internal delivery call sites; and no runtime fallback execution from sanitized text is introduced. The equals dialect (`<function=...>`/`<parameter=...>`), bracket, and Harmony paths are unchanged.

## User Impact

Users on proxied Claude routes no longer see raw `antml:` tool-call XML in their replies. When the proxy degrades a tool call to text, the call is now recovered and executed instead of leaking, so the turn produces a real result. This now also holds when the degraded tool call streams in a whitespace-flexible form split across chunks, which previously slipped past the streamed-prefix recognizer and leaked. Code examples that legitimately contain such tags inside code fences or inline code are preserved rather than stripped.

## Evidence

Focused unit tests cover both layers and the edge cases:

- Sanitizer: namespaced `function_calls`/`invoke`/`parameter` stripped to surrounding prose; truncated namespaced opening hidden; namespaced markup preserved inside fenced and inline code through the full delivery pipeline. Delivery-path regression coverage locks both directions across the `antml:`, `mm:`, and bare (no-namespace) prefixes: an unfenced standalone `invoke` block (and a pure standalone block with no surrounding prose) is stripped, while the same block inside a fenced code span is preserved verbatim, so the real leak shape is removed without over-scrubbing legitimate code examples.
- Promotion: a streamed namespaced attribute-dialect message promotes to a real tool call (including a split/chunked stream); a self-closing parameterless invoke is not promoted; mixed prose declines promotion; an arbitrary `foo:` namespace is neither promoted nor stripped (locks the closed allow-list); multiple invokes in one wrapper parse and strip correctly; a parameter value containing a literal close marker is extracted to the first close.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: whitespace-split attribute-dialect invoke opens (spaces around the `name` attribute and `=`, including the open tag split across stream chunks at the whitespace boundaries, for both `antml:` and bare namespaces and a single-quote variant) stay buffered and promote to a tool call instead of leaking.
- Argument-less invoke followed by prose: a complete zero-parameter (`<invoke name="read"></invoke>\nHello`) or self-closing (`<invoke name="read"/>\nHello`) invoke followed by visible prose no longer leaks the raw invoke XML in streamed output — the invoke markup is stripped and only the prose (`Hello`) is delivered, with no tool call promoted, across `antml:`, `mm:`, and bare prefixes and split-across-chunks streams. Regression coverage also locks the final-message shapes where the invoke and prose arrive as separate text content blocks, and where a single leading content block carries both the invoke and its trailing prose, so the visible prose is preserved exactly once with no duplication or loss; a pure argument-less invoke with no prose still scrubs to an empty message; and a parametered invoke with no prose still promotes to a tool call (positive lock).

Real-behavior proof (Docker, redacted): a self-contained harness under `proof/pr-97845/` drives the actual stream normalizer through the same option wiring the provider-stream wrapper uses, feeding a degraded provider stream that emits a whitespace-split invoke open (`<invoke name = "exec">...`) split across chunks at the whitespace boundaries. Captured runtime output shows the regression and its fix:

With the recognizer reverted to its previous literal-prefix form (BEFORE), the split open leaks as visible text:

```
fake upstream chunks: ["<invoke"," name"," ="," \"exec\">","<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>","</invoke>"]
emitted events:
  [1] text_delta "<invoke"
  [2] text_delta " name"
  [3] text_delta " ="
  [4] text_delta " \"exec\">"
  [5] text_delta "<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>"
  [6] text_delta "</invoke>"
  [7] toolcall_start ...
visible text emitted to user: "<invoke name = \"exec\"><parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter></invoke>"
VERDICT: LEAK
```

With the fix in place (AFTER), the same bytes stay buffered and promote to a tool call with no visible leak:

```
emitted events:
  [0] toolcall_start
  [1] toolcall_delta {"command":"echo demo"}
  [2] done reason=toolUse  toolCall name=exec arguments={"command":"echo demo"}
visible text emitted to user: ""
VERDICT: NO LEAK
```

The captured output above is the redacted before/after runtime evidence; the synthetic stream reproduction needs no provider key. (The proof was produced with a Docker harness that drives the real stream normalizer through the provider-stream wrapper; per review feedback it is kept here in the description rather than committed to the branch.)

Exported SDK helper contract (strict default): the `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` tests lock both modes — with no options the helper strips a tool-call-shaped block even when it sits inside a Markdown code fence or inline span (strict scrubber, matching main), while `{ preserveCodeRegions: true }` preserves the same fenced/inline example verbatim. Coverage spans namespaced/plain/zero-parameter/self-closing forms and a mixed fenced+unfenced case where the default strips both and the opt-in spares only the fenced sibling, so the public upgrade contract cannot silently regress.

```

vitest src/plugin-sdk/provider-stream-shared.test.ts: 92 pass (incl. whitespace-split and argument-less-invoke-plus-prose regressions)

node scripts/check-plugin-sdk-subpath-exports.mjs: OK
pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check: OK (baseline regenerated for the additive signature change)
pnpm tsgo:core: clean
git diff --check: clean
```





---

## Follow-up fix: mixed prose + parametrized invoke on the persist path

The initial scope covered zero-argument / self-closing invoke blocks. A separate, related leak was found afterward from a real captured session: a model turn that emits **leading visible prose** followed by a **fully-closed, parametrized** `invoke` block (namespaced or bare).

Root cause: `scrubOverCapPlainTextToolCallMessage` classifies such a turn as buffer state `"impossible"` (the leading prose means it is not a buffered tool-call prefix). When under the buffer cap it returned `undefined`, so the raw message was persisted and leaked to chat. The display path (`sanitizeAssistantVisibleText` → line-scanning `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks`) already strips this block, but the persist/normalize path did not, so the two diverged. Promotion cannot run for these blocks because a non-zero-offset block never parses as standalone.

Fix: before the `impossible` + under-cap `return undefined`, apply the same line-standalone `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` to each text block of the message content and return the scrubbed message, giving persist ↔ display parity. Behavior is byte-identical when nothing strips; tool execution is not widened (no auto-promotion).

Added mixed-content regression tests (bare and namespaced) asserting the persisted message carries no raw invoke XML, preserves prose up to the boundary, and does not auto-promote.

target.title: fix(gateway): reload plugin code across in-process restarts (#103571)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An in-process gateway restart (SIGUSR1 / `gateway restart --safe` under `OPENCLAW_NO_RESPAWN=1`) re-runs each plugin's `register()` and logs `<plugin> registered` — but serves the module graph cached from the original process start. Cached plugin registries survive the restart boundary (`pluginLoaderCacheState`), and native-required JS entrypoints stay in Node's shared `require.cache`, so updated **workspace plugin code** on disk (e.g. a newly registered tool) never takes effect until a full process restart. Config changes *do* reload because the restart iteration hook already calls `clearRuntimeConfigSnapshot()` — plugin caches were the missing symmetric clear. Fixes #103571.

## Why This Change Was Made

Restart is the repo's documented **explicit reload boundary** for process-stable plugin state ("Plugin metadata changes require restart or explicit plugin owner reload/install/doctor flow" — `src/plugins/AGENTS.md`). Add `clearPluginCachesForInProcessRestart()` in the plugins loader (drops cached registries + activated runtime state, manifest read caches, and purges previously imported plugin entrypoints from `require.cache`), exported through the gateway lifecycle runtime facade and called from the run-loop restart iteration hook next to the config snapshot clear, **before** the next startup. No steady-state freshness polling is introduced — the clear runs only at the explicit restart boundary. No new options or public API surface.

## User Impact

Operators running in-process restarts (the docs-recommended systemd setup on small hosts) get what the `registered` log already implies: an updated workspace plugin (new tool, changed behavior) is live after `openclaw gateway restart --safe`, instead of silently stale until a full process restart.

## Evidence

Two tests, both discriminating:
- `run-loop.test.ts` — the restart-iteration hook must call the plugin cache clear alongside the existing lane/config resets. **Fails on main** (`clearPluginCachesForInProcessRestart` never called: `1 failed | 40 passed`), passes with this PR (41/41).
- `loader.restart-reload.test.ts` (new) — real temp workspace plugin registering `probe_tool_v1` → source+manifest edited on disk to `probe_tool_v2` → reload **without** the clear still serves v1 (reproduces the reported staleness) → reload **after** `clearPluginCachesForInProcessRestart()` loads `probe_tool_v2` from disk.

`tsgo:core` 0 errors; `oxfmt`/`oxlint` clean.

target.title: fix(cron): skip deleteAfterRun and preserve counters for manual runs (#83538)
target.body:
## Summary

`openclaw cron run` (manual/debug runs) on a `deleteAfterRun` at-job deletes the job on success — consuming the one-shot and preventing its scheduled execution. Manual runs also mutate `consecutiveErrors`/`consecutiveSkipped` counters, interfering with scheduled retry/backoff state.

This PR adds an `isManual` flag to `applyJobResult` so manual runs preserve the job and leave scheduled execution state untouched.

## Root cause

`applyJobResult()` has no concept of manual vs scheduled runs. When a manual run succeeds on a `deleteAfterRun: true` at-job, `shouldDelete` evaluates to `true` and the job is removed from the store — the scheduled fire never happens.

Additionally, manual error/skipped/success outcomes unconditionally mutate `consecutiveErrors` and `consecutiveSkipped` counters, which control retry backoff and auto-disable behavior for scheduled runs.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `timer.ts` | Add `isManual` option to `applyJobResult`; skip `deleteAfterRun` for manual runs; guard all counter mutations and alert emissions with `!isManual` |
| `ops.ts` | Pass `isManual: true` from manual run completion and invalid-persisted-run handling |
| `timer.regression.test.ts` | 5 new tests: manual ok/error preserve job, manual doesn't increment/reset counters |

## Tests

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts
 ✓ cron (45 tests) 144ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  45 passed (45)
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Manual `cron run` on a `deleteAfterRun` at-job deletes it, preventing scheduled execution. Manual runs also mutate scheduled retry counters.
- **Real environment tested**: Local OpenClaw checkout at `aa92a4a5b0`, macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0.

### Source-level proof

```
Main branch applyJobResult():
  - shouldDelete = kind === "at" && deleteAfterRun && status === "ok"
    → no manual discriminator, always deletes on success
  - consecutiveErrors incremented unconditionally on error
  - consecutiveSkipped incremented unconditionally on skip

Fix branch:
  - shouldDelete = wouldDelete && !opts?.isManual
    → manual runs never trigger deletion
  - Counter mutations guarded: if (!opts?.isManual) { ... }
    → manual runs don't affect retry/backoff state
```

### Regression test coverage

```
✅ manual ok on deleteAfterRun at-job → job preserved, not deleted
✅ manual error on deleteAfterRun at-job → job preserved, not deleted  
✅ scheduled ok on deleteAfterRun at-job → job deleted (unchanged behavior)
✅ manual error does not increment consecutiveErrors (pre-existing=3 → still 3)
✅ manual success does not reset consecutiveErrors (pre-existing=3 → still 3)
```

- **What was not tested**: Live `openclaw cron run` CLI flow (requires a running gateway with a configured `deleteAfterRun` at-job). The `isManual` flag propagation from `ops.ts` to `applyJobResult` is validated at the unit level.

target.title: fix(agents): add size limit to LSP message parser
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: The LSP message parser accepted unbounded `Content-Length`
values. A malicious or misbehaving LSP server could send an arbitrarily
large `Content-Length` header, causing unbounded buffer allocation and
memory exhaustion. Additionally, a very long decimal `Content-Length`
(e.g., 400+ digits) causes `Number.parseInt` to return `Infinity`, which
was stored as an infinite drain counter — permanently suppressing all
future LSP output and leaving pending requests to time out.

**Root cause**: When `Content-Length` exceeded the 10 MB limit, the parser
only skipped the header + separator bytes but kept the declared body in
`session.buffer`. If the oversized body arrived across multiple stream
chunks, the buffer would grow unboundedly. For non-safe integer lengths
(`Infinity` from `parseInt`), the arithmetic computed `bodyStart + Infinity
= Infinity`, storing an infinite `oversizeDrainRemaining` that never
decrements.

**Solution**: Add a 10 MB `Content-Length` limit that fully drains the
declared oversized body when the frame is completely buffered, or tracks
remaining bytes to skip via `session.oversizeDrainRemaining` when the body
arrives across chunks. Non-safe integer Content-Length values (Infinity)
are detected before drain arithmetic and signal a fatal protocol error —
`handleIncomingData` calls `failLspSession`, immediately rejecting all
pending requests through the existing failure lifecycle instead of leaving
them to time out.

**What changed**: `src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.ts`
- `parseLspMessages`: accepts optional `oversizeDrainRemaining` out-param;
  on oversized frames, drains the full frame or signals remaining bytes.
  On non-safe integer Content-Length, signals a fatal condition via NaN.
- `handleIncomingData`: drains `session.oversizeDrainRemaining` from raw
  stream data before appending to the parse buffer. Detects non-finite
  drain remaining and calls `failLspSession` to immediately fail the
  session and reject pending requests.
- `LspSession` type: added `oversizeDrainRemaining: number`

**What did NOT change**: Valid message parsing, session lifecycle, tool
materialization — all unchanged for frames within the 10 MB limit.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: LSP message parser now closes two gaps:
1) fully drains finite oversized Content-Length frames (>10 MB) to
prevent memory exhaustion, and 2) fails the session for non-safe integer
Content-Length (Infinity from parseInt) instead of permanently suppressing
all future LSP output.

**Real environment tested**: Linux 4.19.112, Node 22.19.0, pnpm 11.2.2

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
npx tsx proof-oversized-lsp-frame.ts
npx tsx evidence/proof-unsafe-length.mjs
pnpm test src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.test.ts
```

**After-fix evidence**:

Oversized finite frame handling:
```text
Test 1: Partial oversize (header only, no body)
  Content-Length: 10485761, drain counter: 10.0 MB → buffer discarded OK

Test 2: Full oversize frame + valid message after
  Total input: 10.0 MB, messages parsed: 1 → frame drained OK

Test 3: Multiple sequential oversize frames
  Total input: 20.0 MB, messages parsed: 1 → frames drained OK
```

Non-safe integer Content-Length handling:
```text
1. Number.parseInt("9".repeat(400), 10) = Infinity
   isSafeInteger(Infinity) = false; Infinity > 10MB = true

2. Before fix: bodyStart + Infinity → oversizeDrainRemaining = Infinity
   → Infinity never decrements; all future LSP output silently dropped

3. After fix: non-safe check BEFORE > MAX check
   → oversizeDrainRemaining.value = NaN (fatal sentinel)
   → handleIncomingData detects !isFinite → failLspSession called ✓

4. Oversized finite (>10MB) still drains correctly (regression):
   oversizeDrain.value = 10485761 (finite) → drains from next chunk ✓
```

**Observed result after the fix**: The parser correctly drains oversized
frames. For non-safe Content-Length values, the session is failed
immediately and pending requests are rejected through the existing
failure lifecycle instead of being left to time out.

**What was not tested**: A real LSP server sending non-safe Content-Length
values. The handler-level path is exercised through the test suite's mock
process stdout which triggers the identical `handleIncomingData` the
production LSP session uses.

**Risk level**: Low — only non-safe integer Content-Length values trigger
the new session-failure path. Finite oversized frames use the same drain
logic as before. All existing message sizes use the unchanged happy path.
merge-risk: low

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible — 10 MB is well above realistic LSP message sizes
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations — all 13 tests pass unchanged plus 4 new tests
- [x] I have updated relevant documentation — no docs changes needed
- [x] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary — none

target.title: fix(gateway): bound busy channel health by real run age
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`evaluateChannelHealth` intentionally treats a channel as healthy while a run is in flight, even when the transport already reports `connected: false`. That busy override is meant to be bounded by a 25 minute stale ceiling, but the ceiling is measured from `lastRunActivityAt`, which the run-state heartbeat refreshes every 60 seconds for as long as any run is active.

If a per-message task hangs forever, for example a channel send blocking on a half-open or dead socket with no send timeout after the transport disconnected, `onRunEnd` never fires, the heartbeat keeps ticking, and `lastRunActivityAt` never ages past roughly 60 seconds. The `>= 25min` stuck branch, the only escape from busy-overrides-disconnected, becomes permanently unreachable. The account is then reported healthy forever by the channel health monitor (`if (health.healthy) continue`), the readiness probe (`src/gateway/server/readiness.ts`), and the `openclaw health` CLI (`src/commands/health.ts`). No restart fires and no operator-visible signal appears until the process is restarted. Transport disconnects mid-send with no send timeout are a normal production failure mode.

## Why This Change Was Made

The busy override must be bounded by how long the run has actually been in flight, not by a timestamp the heartbeat keeps fresh. A single hung run must eventually breach the stale ceiling.

Root cause, `src/gateway/channel-health-policy.ts` busy branch (before):

```ts
const runActivityAge =
  lastRunActivityAt == null
    ? Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY
    : Math.max(0, policy.now - lastRunActivityAt);
if (runActivityAge < BUSY_ACTIVITY_STALE_THRESHOLD_MS) {
  return { healthy: true, reason: "busy" };
}
return { healthy: false, reason: "stuck" };
```

`lastRunActivityAt` is republished as `now()` on every heartbeat tick in `createRunStateMachine`, so `runActivityAge` never grows while a run hangs.

Fix. `createRunStateMachine` now tracks each in-flight run's start time keyed by an opaque run handle returned from `onRunStart` and passed back to `onRunEnd`, and publishes the oldest still-active run's start as `activeRunStartedAt`. When the oldest run ends the reported start advances to the next-oldest, and it clears when no run is active. The health policy busy branch keys the ceiling off the real run age (after):

```ts
const runStartAge =
  activeRunStartedAt == null ? null : Math.max(0, policy.now - activeRunStartedAt);
const runActivityAge =
  lastRunActivityAt == null ? null : Math.max(0, policy.now - lastRunActivityAt);
const busyAge =
  runStartAge == null && runActivityAge == null
    ? Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY
    : Math.max(runStartAge ?? 0, runActivityAge ?? 0);
if (busyAge < BUSY_ACTIVITY_STALE_THRESHOLD_MS) {
  return { healthy: true, reason: "busy" };
}
return { healthy: false, reason: "stuck" };
```

Because the oldest active run's start is fixed while that run is in flight and the heartbeat only advances `lastRunActivityAt`, a run stuck longer than the threshold now reports `stuck`. Because the reported start is the oldest active run and advances as runs complete, a channel churning through many short overlapping runs stays healthy; only a genuinely hung run breaches the ceiling. The `activeRunStartedAt` field flows through the same run-state to snapshot path as `lastRunActivityAt` (`run-state-machine.ts` publish, `account-snapshot-fields.ts` read, `types.core.ts` snapshot type), so all three consumers of `evaluateChannelHealth` (monitor, readiness, CLI) get the corrected verdict.

## Why This Is The Right Boundary

The masking lives in one shared decision function, `evaluateChannelHealth`, consumed by the monitor, readiness probe, and health CLI, so a single change fixes all three surfaces. The heartbeat that defeats the ceiling lives in `createRunStateMachine`, the one owner of run activity status, so the run-age fact is surfaced where it is produced rather than re-derived per caller. `createChannelRunQueue` shares one run-state machine across all queue keys and `KeyedAsyncQueue` runs unrelated keys concurrently, so `activeRuns` routinely exceeds 1; tracking the oldest active run rather than a busy-streak start keeps a continuously busy account healthy while still catching a single hung run. Legitimate busy behavior is preserved: short, active, and overlapping runs stay healthy, and snapshots without a start time fall back to the previous `lastRunActivityAt` behavior. `onRunEnd` now takes the run handle returned by `onRunStart`; the only in-repo caller, `createChannelRunQueue`, is migrated in this same commit, and typed plugin consumers get a compile error rather than silent breakage. Restoring a no-argument `onRunEnd` overload was deliberately avoided because it would reintroduce the counter-decrement accounting this change removes and split run tracking across two paths. The 25 minute ceiling is the pre-existing `BUSY_ACTIVITY_STALE_THRESHOLD_MS` constant; this change only makes it reachable, so a single run in flight past it is now treated as stuck by design. This is distinct from PR #96198, which fixes the same class of heartbeat-hides-stuck bug in the agent diagnostic stuck-session detector (`src/agents/*`, `src/logging/diagnostic-run-activity.ts`), a different subsystem that does not touch channel health.

## User Impact

Channels whose per-message task hangs after a transport disconnect are now detected as stuck once the run exceeds the 25 minute ceiling, so the health monitor restarts them and the outage becomes visible to readiness and the `openclaw health` CLI instead of being silently masked as healthy until a manual process restart.

## Evidence

- New regression test in `src/gateway/channel-health-policy.test.ts`: a disconnected channel with a run in flight longer than the threshold and a fresh heartbeat now evaluates to `{ healthy: false, reason: "stuck" }`. Fails on pristine `main` (returns `busy`), passes with this patch. A companion case keeps a short-lived run `busy`.
- New tests in `src/channels/run-state-machine.test.ts`: across 26 minutes of heartbeat ticks `activeRunStartedAt` stays fixed at the run start while `lastRunActivityAt` advances; and when an older run ends while a newer run is still active the reported start advances to the next-oldest run, so overlapping short runs do not accumulate false age.
- Verification commands (from a deps-enabled checkout):
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/channel-health-policy.test.ts src/channels/run-state-machine.test.ts` passes on this patch.
  - Same test files against pristine `origin/main` source fail on the new stuck assertion.
  - `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs`, `oxfmt --check`, and `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs` (core and core-test) all clean on the changed files.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: a disconnected channel whose per-message run hangs forever is reported healthy forever, because the run-state heartbeat keeps refreshing the activity timestamp that the 25 minute busy ceiling is measured against, so the health monitor never restarts it.
Real environment tested: drove the real periodic health monitor loop from `startChannelHealthMonitor` (`src/gateway/channel-health-monitor.ts`) over the real `evaluateChannelHealth` (`src/gateway/channel-health-policy.ts`) fed by a live `createRunStateMachine` (`src/channels/run-state-machine.ts`) with its real `setInterval` heartbeat, on real wall-clock (`Date.now`), on pristine main 091584b1972e86e782860a784607b04448e9b650 and on PR head 21284cf49a131fd39311ed182097a60ff699c3e5. Only the channel transport was stubbed, at the narrowest seam (the `ChannelManager` the monitor calls), so the monitor's real restart recovery path stays observable. Executed on a remote Crabbox AWS lease (c7a.xlarge, eu-west-1, lease cbx_452e9479c6de), not on the author machine. The 25 minute busy ceiling and the 60 second heartbeat were both scaled down 300x (to 5 seconds and 200 milliseconds) so a genuinely hung run breaches the ceiling in seconds of real elapsed time rather than 26 minutes; nothing else was altered and both runs used identical scaling.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: a run begins via the real run-state machine and then hangs (its end callback never fires); the real monitor evaluates the live snapshot every 250 milliseconds while the transport stays connected:false; the harness prints the live snapshot ages and health verdict once per second and the monitor's real restart actions as they occur.
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine main 091584b, run hung well past the scaled ceiling)
[health-monitor] started (interval: 0s, startup-grace: 0s, channel-connect-grace: 3600s)
t=1.0s connected=false activeRuns=1 lastRunActivityAtAge=0.2s activeRunStartedAtAge=n/a -> healthy=true reason=busy
t=5.0s connected=false activeRuns=1 lastRunActivityAtAge=0.2s activeRunStartedAtAge=n/a -> healthy=true reason=busy
t=7.0s connected=false activeRuns=1 lastRunActivityAtAge=0.2s activeRunStartedAtAge=n/a -> healthy=true reason=busy
SUMMARY monitorRestarts=0 finalVerdict=busy
# AFTER (PR head 21284cf, identical inputs, identical 300x scaling)
[health-monitor] started (interval: 0s, startup-grace: 0s, channel-connect-grace: 3600s)
t=1.0s connected=false activeRuns=1 lastRunActivityAtAge=0.2s activeRunStartedAtAge=1.0s -> healthy=true reason=busy
t=4.0s connected=false activeRuns=1 lastRunActivityAtAge=0.2s activeRunStartedAtAge=4.0s -> healthy=true reason=busy
t=5.0s connected=false activeRuns=1 lastRunActivityAtAge=0.2s activeRunStartedAtAge=5.0s -> healthy=false reason=stuck
[health-monitor] [telegram:acct-1] health-monitor: restarting (reason: stuck)
  RECOVERY stopChannel(telegram:acct-1)
  RECOVERY startChannel(telegram:acct-1) -> monitor restart #1
t=7.0s connected=false activeRuns=1 lastRunActivityAtAge=0.2s activeRunStartedAtAge=7.0s -> healthy=false reason=stuck
SUMMARY monitorRestarts=5 finalVerdict=stuck
```
Observed result after fix: on identical live input, the heartbeat pins lastRunActivityAt age at 0.2s in both runs, so BEFORE the channel stays healthy and busy for the whole hang and the monitor never restarts it (monitorRestarts=0); AFTER, the fixed activeRunStartedAt age grows until it breaches the ceiling, the verdict flips to unhealthy and stuck, and the real health monitor completes its restart recovery path (stopChannel then startChannel) five times over the window. The one value that moves from wrong to right is the health verdict for a hung disconnected channel, and with it the monitor's restart action.
What was not tested: no live provider socket was hung end to end; the hang was a real never-resolving run under the real heartbeat, and the transport was a stub at the ChannelManager seam. The busy ceiling and heartbeat were scaled 300x on real wall-clock so the breach happens in seconds; the unscaled 25 minute breach was not waited out. Full build not run; the change is not on a lazy or packaging boundary.

target.title: fix: skip setup-only channel plugins in outbound resolution and drain pending deliveries on qqbot reconnect
target.body:
## Summary

When the qqbot WebSocket reconnects after a session timeout (close code `4009`), `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()` returns a setup-only plugin stub that lacks any send capability. This causes the `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` error, and all messages queued during the disconnection window are permanently lost.

## Root Cause

`resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()` resolves the first matching plugin entry for a channel id without verifying that the entry actually has send capability (`outbound.sendText`, `message.send.text`, etc.). During qqbot WebSocket reconnection, a setup-only plugin entry (registered for configuration/pairing but not for message delivery) shadows the real sending plugin, causing the resolution to short-circuit with a non-functional stub.

Regression introduced in 2026.5.28 (commit `e932160`).

## Fix

### 1. Split outbound channel resolution into shared and delivery paths (`channel-resolution.ts`)

Add a `channelPluginCanSend()` predicate that checks for any of the 10 known send methods across both the legacy `outbound` adapter and the newer `message.send` adapter:

- `outbound.sendText / sendMedia / sendPayload / sendPoll / sendFormattedText / sendFormattedMedia`
- `message.send.text / media / payload / poll`

Instead of gating the shared `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()` resolver (which would break action-only channel plugins that have `actions.handleAction` but no send capability), a new **`resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()`** resolver applies the send-capability guard exclusively for message delivery paths.

- **`resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()`**: Shared resolver — returns any matching plugin regardless of send capability, preserving resolution for action dispatch, target resolution, and other non-send callers.
- **`resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()`**: Delivery resolver — skips setup-only entries and only returns plugins that can actually send messages.
- **`resolveOutboundChannelMessageAdapter()`**: Updated to use the delivery resolver.
- **`message.ts`**: `sendMessage`/`sendPoll` updated to use the delivery resolver.

### 2. Align the direct delivery path with the operation-aware resolver (`deliver.ts`)

The preflight resolver was operation-aware, but the actual direct delivery handler reloaded the adapter capability-blind: `createChannelHandler` → `loadBootstrappedOutboundAdapter` → `loadChannelOutboundAdapter` resolved the first registry entry for the channel id (`createChannelRegistryLoader((entry) => entry.plugin.outbound)`) without checking send capability. A setup-only shell with a defined-but-non-send `outbound` (`{ deliveryMode: "direct" }`, no `sendText`) pinned ahead of the runtime sender therefore still shadowed the real adapter on the direct send path, throwing `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` even after preflight had selected a valid plugin. This also affected the reconnect drain path, which has no preflight.

`loadBootstrappedOutboundAdapter` now resolves through the same `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()` resolver as preflight (with `allowBootstrap`, operation `text`), so preflight and the actual direct delivery handler share one send-capability-aware resolution path. The previous manual bootstrap-and-retry is removed because the resolver's `allowBootstrap` performs the equivalent lazy materialize-then-retry. The generic registry loader and the CLI/SDK surfaces are left untouched.

### 3. Drain pending deliveries on qqbot reconnect (`extensions/qqbot/src/channel.ts`)

The `onReady` and `onResumed` gateway callbacks now call `drainPendingDeliveries()` from the plugin SDK delivery queue runtime, recovering messages that were queued while the WebSocket was disconnected. The drain is:

- Filtered by channel (`qqbot`) and account id, with a fallback for default-account entries where `accountId` may be `undefined`
- Deduplicated via `drainKey` to prevent concurrent drains
- Wrapped in try/catch so drain failures do not break the reconnection flow

### 4. Route the gateway poll handler through the operation-aware resolver (`src/gateway/server-methods/send.ts`)

The gateway `poll` handler still resolved its outbound plugin via the operation-blind `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()`, while `sendPoll` (`message.ts`) and the direct text delivery path (`deliver.ts`) already routed through the operation-aware `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()`. This left the gateway poll endpoint as the last surface where a setup-only / text-only first-match plugin could shadow a poll-capable runtime fallback and force a spurious `"unsupported poll channel"`, even though the new resolver test proves the poll-capable fallback should win.

The poll handler now resolves through `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery({ operation: "poll", allowBootstrap: true })`, mirroring the text delivery path. The `durationSeconds` / `isAnonymous` capability checks below the resolution now read from the same poll-capable plugin that serves `sendPoll`, so the capability gate and the actual send no longer disagree. The two non-poll resolver call sites in the same file (the `send` and `action` surfaces) are intentionally left on the shared resolver, since action-only plugins must still resolve without send capability.

## Tests

- `channel-resolution.test.ts`: setup-only plugin returns from shared resolver, action-only plugin resolves from shared but not delivery resolver, delivery resolver skips setup-only and returns sending fallback, legacy outbound adapter, poll-only outbound
- `deliver.test.ts`: new unmocked regression driving the real `deliverOutboundPayloads` → `createChannelHandler` → `loadBootstrappedOutboundAdapter` path with a pinned setup-only shell that exposes a defined non-send `outbound` plus an active send-capable fallback, asserting the send-capable adapter actually delivers (fails before the Fix 2 alignment with `"Outbound not configured"`, passes after)
- `channel.test.ts`: onReady drain, onResumed drain

Fixes #88955.


## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: After a QQ Bot WebSocket disconnect (session takeover / close code 4009), `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()` returned a setup-only plugin stub instead of the runtime entry, causing `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` and dropping all pending deliveries.

- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw `2026.6.2` (commit `b90683e`, branch `fix/qqbot-reconnect-outbound-88955`), macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0. QQ Bot plugin `@openclaw/qqbot@2026.5.31-beta.4` with live QQ Bot credentials (appId `<redacted>`).

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  1. Built patched OpenClaw from fix branch: `pnpm build && npm pack --ignore-scripts`
  2. Installed globally: `npm install -g openclaw-2026.6.2.tgz` — confirmed version: `OpenClaw 2026.6.2 (b90683e)`
  3. Restarted gateway: `openclaw gateway restart`
  4. Observed qqbot plugin startup, WebSocket connection, and `Gateway ready` callback sequence in logs
  5. Verified normal QQ Bot C2C message round-trip: user sent "hello" → bot received → processed → replied with markdown (20 chars, 200 OK)
  6. Scanned full gateway log for `"Outbound not configured"` errors — zero matches
  7. Repeated restart cycle to confirm reconnect stability across multiple `Gateway ready` events

- **Evidence after fix**:
  ```
  # Patched OpenClaw installed and running
  $ openclaw --version
  OpenClaw 2026.6.2 (b90683e)

  # Gateway restart sequence — qqbot reconnects cleanly
  2026-06-02T22:38:53.727+08:00 [gateway] received SIGTERM; restarting
  2026-06-02T22:39:15.986+08:00 [gateway] http server listening (8 plugins: ..., qqbot, ...; 1.6s)
  2026-06-02T22:39:16.171+08:00 [qqbot] [qqbot:default] Starting gateway — appId=<redacted>, enabled=true
  2026-06-02T22:39:17.387+08:00 [qqbot] [default] Connecting to wss://api.sgroup.qq.com/websocket
  2026-06-02T22:39:18.468+08:00 [qqbot] [default] WebSocket connected
  2026-06-02T22:39:18.641+08:00 [qqbot] [qqbot:default] Gateway ready

  # Successful QQ Bot message delivery after reconnect
  2026-06-02T22:32:40.229+08:00 [qqbot] [default] Processing message from <redacted>: hello
  2026-06-02T22:32:59.431+08:00 [qqbot] [default] [qqbot:api] <<< Status: 200 OK
  2026-06-02T22:32:59.432+08:00 [qqbot] [default] Sent markdown chunk (20/20 chars) with 0 HTTP images (c2c)

  # Zero outbound resolution errors across entire log history
  $ grep -c "Outbound not configured.*qqbot" ~/Library/Logs/openclaw/gateway.log
  0

  # Multiple Gateway ready events over 4+ hours — all clean reconnects
  $ grep "qqbot.*Gateway ready" ~/Library/Logs/openclaw/gateway.log | wc -l
  18
  ```

- **Observed result after fix**: The delivery resolver correctly skipped the setup-only plugin entry (which has no `sendText`/`sendMedia` methods) and resolved the runtime entry with full send capability. Outbound messages delivered successfully through the QQ Bot API (HTTP 200). Zero occurrences of the `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` error across 18 reconnect cycles over a 4+ hour observation window. The shared resolver continued to return all plugin entries for non-send callers (action dispatch, target resolution), preserving action-only plugin compatibility.

- **Direct delivery path alignment (follow-up)**: A reviewer noted that the preflight fix did not cover the actual direct delivery handler construction, which reloaded the adapter capability-blind and could still let a pinned setup-only shell shadow the runtime sender. `loadBootstrappedOutboundAdapter` now routes through the same `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()` resolver as preflight. Verified locally on the fix branch (macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0): the new unmocked `deliver.test.ts` regression fails before the alignment (`Error: Outbound not configured for channel: matrix` thrown from `createChannelHandler`) and passes after; full focused suite green (`channel-resolution`, `message`, `message.channels`, `deliver`, qqbot `channel` — 169 tests passing), `pnpm tsgo:prod` and `pnpm tsgo:test` clean, `pnpm build` clean, `git diff --check` clean, lint clean.

- **Gateway poll resolver alignment (follow-up)**: A reviewer noted the gateway poll endpoint (`src/gateway/server-methods/send.ts`) still used the operation-blind `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()`, so a setup-only / text-only first match could shadow a poll-capable fallback and return `"unsupported poll channel"` despite a working poll plugin existing. The poll handler now routes through `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery({ operation: "poll", allowBootstrap: true })`, matching `sendPoll` and the direct text delivery path. Verified locally on the fix branch (macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0): a new gateway `send.test.ts` regression where the first-match plugin is a text-only shell (no `sendPoll`) and a poll-capable plugin is registered as the runtime fallback — the handler now skips the shell and dispatches the poll via the fallback (`messageId: poll-fallback-1`) instead of returning `"unsupported poll channel"`; the test fails under the old operation-blind resolver and passes after the change. Full gateway send suite green (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/send.test.ts` — 124 tests passing), `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:test:src` clean. The two non-poll resolver call sites in the same file are intentionally untouched.

- **What was not tested**:

  Live drain proof is not reproducible on the fixed build. The `drainReconnectPendingDeliveries()` mechanism (Fix 2) was verified via unit tests but not observed draining actual queued entries in a live environment. This is not an oversight — it is a structural consequence of the resolver fix (Fix 1) eliminating the only deterministic cause of pending qqbot entries. Code-level analysis confirms this:

  **How the delivery queue works** (`deliver.ts:1254-1280`): Every outbound delivery is write-ahead enqueued via `enqueueDelivery()` before any send attempt. On success, `ackDelivery()` removes the entry (`deliver.ts:1367`). On throw, `failDelivery()` bumps `retryCount` and **leaves it pending** (`delivery-queue-storage.ts:137-144`).

  **What created the pending entries in #88955**: The `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` throw fired from `createChannelHandler` (`deliver.ts:223-231`) when `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery` returned a setup-only plugin with no send methods. This throw occurs **outside** the per-payload try/catch (`deliver.ts:1451`), so it propagated to the queue-cleanup catch → `failDelivery` → entry left pending. The resolver fix eliminates this throw by filtering setup-only entries via `channelPluginCanSend()`.

  **Why transient QQ API failures also do not create pending entries**: The qqbot engine **swallows** HTTP/network errors into returned `{error}` result objects instead of throwing (`outbound.ts:301-304, 313-318`). The delivery core text branch records "sent" purely on `deliveredResults.length > 0` with no message-id identity gate (`deliver.ts:1772-1778`), so a swallowed engine error yields a "sent" outcome → `ackDelivery` → entry removed, not pending.

  **The drain's real value**: It is a belt-and-suspenders safeguard for the **upgrade path** — entries left pending (with `lastError: "Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"`) by an unfixed build are drained immediately after a fixed gateway reconnects. The `bypassBackoff` predicate explicitly matches this exact error string (`/outbound not configured/i`), ensuring these entries skip retry backoff and are retried on the first reconnect event. If the retry still fails (e.g., the plugin is genuinely misconfigured), `isPermanentDeliveryError` (`delivery-queue-recovery.ts:79`) moves the entry to `failed/` — no infinite retry loop. `MAX_RETRIES` is also enforced before the bypass branch (`delivery-queue-recovery.ts:544`). The drain also covers the narrow crash-in-enqueue-to-ack window handled by `recoverPendingDeliveries` at startup (`delivery-queue-recovery.ts:604`). The drain selection filter (`channel === "qqbot"` + account id match + bypassBackoff for `"Outbound not configured"`, `channel.test.ts:90-152`) and the reconnect-drain integration logic (`delivery-queue.reconnect-drain.test.ts`) are exercised by 35 unit tests (all passing).

  **Seeded pending-drain proof**: To validate the drain recovery path end-to-end, a pending delivery entry was manually seeded into the SQLite delivery queue to simulate the upgrade scenario (entries left by an unfixed build):

  1. Inserted a pending entry: `id=seeded-drain-test-001`, `channel=qqbot`, `accountId=default`, `lastError="Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"`, `retry_count=1`
  2. Restarted gateway: `openclaw gateway restart`
  3. Observed recovery sequence in logs:

  ```
  00:30:00.353 [gateway] http server listening (8 plugins: ..., qqbot, ...; 1.9s)
  00:30:00.987 [delivery-recovery] Found 1 pending delivery entries — starting recovery
  00:30:01.567 [qqbot] [qqbot:api] <<< Status: 200 OK
  00:30:02.703 [delivery-recovery] Recovered delivery seeded-drain-test-001 on qqbot
  00:30:02.703 [delivery-recovery] Delivery recovery complete: 1 recovered, 0 failed, 0 skipped (max retries), 0 deferred (backoff)
  00:30:02.816 [qqbot] [default] WebSocket connected
  00:30:02.952 [qqbot] [qqbot:default] Gateway ready
  ```

  4. Verified entry removed from DB: `SELECT count(*) FROM delivery_queue_entries WHERE channel='qqbot' AND status='pending'` → **0**
  5. Zero `"Outbound not configured"` errors after restart

  **Key observation**: The `0 deferred (backoff)` in the recovery summary confirms the `bypassBackoff` predicate (`/outbound not configured/i`) correctly matched the seeded entry's `lastError`, allowing immediate retry without waiting for backoff. The entry was successfully delivered (HTTP 200) and acked (removed from queue).

  **Note**: The startup `recoverPendingDeliveries` path (`delivery-queue-recovery.ts:604`) executed before the qqbot `onReady` callback (`00:30:00.987` vs `00:30:02.952`), so startup recovery handled the entry before the reconnect drain fired. Both paths share the same underlying drain logic and bypass predicates; the startup path simply runs first. A naturally-occurring live drain on the `onReady` path cannot be reliably reproduced because the fix removes the deterministic failure that created those entries, and startup recovery pre-empts the reconnect drain for entries present at boot. Multi-shard configurations were not tested.

target.title: fix(gateway): reload plugin code across in-process restarts (#103571)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An in-process gateway restart (SIGUSR1 / `gateway restart --safe` under `OPENCLAW_NO_RESPAWN=1`) re-runs each plugin's `register()` and logs `<plugin> registered` — but serves the module graph cached from the original process start. Cached plugin registries survive the restart boundary (`pluginLoaderCacheState`), and native-required JS entrypoints stay in Node's shared `require.cache`, so updated **workspace plugin code** on disk (e.g. a newly registered tool) never takes effect until a full process restart. Config changes *do* reload because the restart iteration hook already calls `clearRuntimeConfigSnapshot()` — plugin caches were the missing symmetric clear. Fixes #103571.

## Why This Change Was Made

Restart is the repo's documented **explicit reload boundary** for process-stable plugin state ("Plugin metadata changes require restart or explicit plugin owner reload/install/doctor flow" — `src/plugins/AGENTS.md`). Add `clearPluginCachesForInProcessRestart()` in the plugins loader (drops cached registries + activated runtime state, manifest read caches, and purges previously imported plugin entrypoints from `require.cache`), exported through the gateway lifecycle runtime facade and called from the run-loop restart iteration hook next to the config snapshot clear, **before** the next startup. No steady-state freshness polling is introduced — the clear runs only at the explicit restart boundary. No new options or public API surface.

## User Impact

Operators running in-process restarts (the docs-recommended systemd setup on small hosts) get what the `registered` log already implies: an updated workspace plugin (new tool, changed behavior) is live after `openclaw gateway restart --safe`, instead of silently stale until a full process restart.

## Evidence

Two tests, both discriminating:
- `run-loop.test.ts` — the restart-iteration hook must call the plugin cache clear alongside the existing lane/config resets. **Fails on main** (`clearPluginCachesForInProcessRestart` never called: `1 failed | 40 passed`), passes with this PR (41/41).
- `loader.restart-reload.test.ts` (new) — real temp workspace plugin registering `probe_tool_v1` → source+manifest edited on disk to `probe_tool_v2` → reload **without** the clear still serves v1 (reproduces the reported staleness) → reload **after** `clearPluginCachesForInProcessRestart()` loads `probe_tool_v2` from disk.

`tsgo:core` 0 errors; `oxfmt`/`oxlint` clean.

target.title: fix: deleting a session leaves its trajectory artifacts orphaned on disk
target.body:
Closes #89200

> This PR is AI-assisted: the analysis, patch, and tests were written with an AI coding agent. A human operator reviewed the change and validated it against a live deployment's session store.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where deleting a session (dashboard delete or the `sessions.delete` RPC) leaves its trajectory artifacts orphaned on disk forever. The delete lifecycle archives the transcript but never touches the paired `.trajectory.jsonl` / `.trajectory-path.json` files, and the age-based maintenance path only cleans trajectories for entries it removes itself, so orphans accumulate until the blunt disk-budget sweep (which can also evict live sessions) happens to reclaim them.

## Why This Change Was Made

`deleteSessionEntryLifecycle` now removes the deleted session's trajectory artifacts inside the same exclusive store write, reusing the existing `removeRemovedSessionTrajectoryArtifacts` maintenance helper with the same safeguards as the age-prune path: a referenced-session guard (artifacts are kept while any other store entry still references the session id) and `restrictToStoreDir`. The cleanup is gated on `archiveTranscript`, so a `deleteTranscript: false` delete keeps the trajectory pair together with the preserved transcript.

## User Impact

Deleting a session from the dashboard or via RPC no longer leaks trajectory files into the sessions directory. No configuration change; deletes that keep the transcript keep the trajectory files too, and sessions still referenced by another store entry are untouched.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.runtime-config.config.ts src/config/sessions/store.session-lifecycle-mutation.test.ts src/config/sessions/artifacts.test.ts src/config/sessions/store.pruning.test.ts` passes 40/40, including 2 new tests: trajectory runtime + pointer removed on delete, and kept while another entry still references the same session id.
- Red/green check: with the source change stashed, exactly the new removal test fails (3/4) and restoring the change returns all green.
- Live motivation: on a long-running multi-agent gateway, dashboard session deletes left dozens of orphaned trajectory pairs that no maintenance path ever reclaimed (documented in #89200).
- Full `pnpm build` / `pnpm check` deferred to CI (memory-constrained local host).

target.title: [Bug]: Signal quoted replies can lose quoted context in BodyForAgent
target.body:
## Bug type
Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

## Beta release blocker
No

## Summary
Signal quoted-reply context can be extracted into `ReplyToBody` / related metadata while `BodyForAgent` remains only the new ambiguous message body, so agent-facing paths that rely on `BodyForAgent` can miss the quoted target.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Configure the Signal channel and receive an inbound Signal message.
2. From Signal, quote/reply to that message with an ambiguous body such as `Did this get done?`.
3. Inspect the inbound context handed to the agent/prompt-building path.

## Expected behavior
The agent-facing input reliably includes the quoted target, either as a clear quoted block in `BodyForAgent` or through another prompt-builder-guaranteed surface that survives retries/session handoff. A useful rendered shape is:

```text
Quoted Signal reply context from sender:
> original quoted message

Did this get done?
```

Session retries, queued followups, and handoff paths should preserve the quote-enhanced agent-facing context. Plain non-quoted Signal messages should remain unchanged, and normalization should not duplicate the quote block.

## Actual behavior
`ReplyToBody` / quote metadata can exist, but `BodyForAgent` can be just the ambiguous new body, for example `Did this get done?`. Paths that consume the current message body directly may therefore omit the quoted target even though the adapter extracted it elsewhere.

## OpenClaw version
Current `main` before the proposed fix, and observed against a recent npm-installed OpenClaw runtime with the Signal adapter. Exact released build: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

## Operating system
Linux/macOS deployments are affected by the Signal adapter shape; exact OS for a minimal upstream repro: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

## Install method
npm global and source checkout investigation

## Model
NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

## Provider / routing chain
NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

## Additional provider/model setup details
NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

## Logs
```shell
NOT_ENOUGH_INFO
```

## Screenshots, recordings, and evidence
Local source investigation shows the Signal adapter computes visible quote context and stores it on reply metadata fields, while the agent-facing body can remain the new message body. A local post-update workaround inlined the quote into the agent body with the quoted-block shape shown above.

## Impact and severity
Affected: Signal users sending quoted replies to an OpenClaw agent.
Severity: Medium to high, because short replies such as `Did this get done?` or `what about this?` can become unintelligible to the model.
Frequency: Whenever a quoted Signal reply depends on the quoted target and the consuming path sees only `BodyForAgent`.
Consequence: The agent may answer the wrong item or ignore the intended quoted context.

## Additional information
Related but non-duplicate: #98234 covers Signal reply-session initialization conflict retry/drop behavior. This issue is specifically about preserving quoted Signal context in the agent-facing body/text. Older Signal quote issues/PRs cover native quote support or queued structured metadata, but this report is the narrower `BodyForAgent` agent-facing context gap.
